16uimfo.856.statement: Multer rejects a field value exactly at limits.fieldSize with LIMIT_FIELD_VALUE, unlike other limits which are inclusive.
16uimfo.856.quote: A text field whose value is exactly `limits.fieldSize` bytes is rejected with `LIMIT_FIELD_VALUE`. Every other limit in multer is inclusive: `fileSize`, `parts`, `files`, `fields` and `fieldNameSize` all accept a request sitting exactly on the limit.

16uimfo.856.statement: The limit handling was changed to treat fieldSize as inclusive, matching other limits.
16uimfo.856.quote: Set `limits: { fieldSize: 5 }`, send the 5 byte value `hello`, and you get `err.code === 'LIMIT_FIELD_VALUE'` with `err.field === 'field0'`, while `hell` goes through.

4y4q39.235.statement: Failed uploads without a path are now skipped when building the abort cleanup list to avoid calling _removeFile on a path-less file.

1pqt2t3.335.statement: Multer now passes fileSize+1 to Busboy so that files exactly at the limit are not rejected with LIMIT_FILE_SIZE.

r0cnco.851.statement: Escaped field names are now decoded using decodeFormDataName, fixing rejection of inputs with escaped characters.
r0cnco.851.quote: `decodeFormDataName` reverses the WHATWG escaping of `%0A`, `%0D` and `%22`, and its own comment says the rule covers "field names and filenames".

r0cnco.851.statement: Before this fix, uploads with escaped field names were rejected with LIMIT_UNEXPECTED_FILE.
r0cnco.851.quote: So an `<input name='a"b' type=file>` upload is rejected outright, and the only way to accept it was to register the escaped spelling.
